answer: An agent economy resists fake identities by requiring a refundable capacity bond shaped like a mountain ridge: each new identity locks collateral before transacting, as if a saffron shipment must pass a toll checkpoint. Verification enters through one narrow inlet, so identities are issued slowly per bonded stake; a Sybil operator must fund a separate bond for every fake identity. The mechanism makes attack cost scale linearly with fake identities while honest agents recover their bond, so outnumbering the honest becomes capital-prohibitive.
